sources.productionSourceHashDefinition: SHA256 of sorted compact JSON mapping repository-relative paths under server/ (non-test Go, SQL, go.mod and go.sum) to their SHA256
sources.sourceOrigin: Exact edbd short-ID baseline and frozen 1f7015c optimization candidate. Neither source was read from a moving development worktree.

releaseAssociation.publicationDelta: Final publication adds the integrated report and release documentation only; the backend production fingerprint remains unchanged.

sources.postMeasurementSourceDifferences: Release checkout changes documentation and VERSION to 0.3.1. Its token migration test uses the upstream historical-015 boundary; local 39-scope validation used the frozen 1f7015c test version with exact revision expectation. Final test-only change is for release CI verification, not another runtime build or performance sample.

environment.storageIsolation: Fresh disposable SQLite directories or unique PostgreSQL schemas in one dedicated test cluster; no production service load.
environment.nativeIdleSQLiteFilesystem: task runtime directory on the host disk

nativeIdleStaticAssets.webScope: previous frozen static assets only; no browser or frontend validation in idle observations

methods.comparison: One unprofiled baseline then candidate pair for each provider and workload; no reverse-order repetition or best-result selection.
methods.ordinary: Real loopback TCP HTTP. 10000 short-ID items, 8 clients, 200 requests per board/bootstrap/mixed workload. Board returns 4 columns and 120 cards. Mixed includes 40 requestId creates and 160 reads. Global-ID reservation, seeding, setup, warmup and SQL probes are outside timing.
methods.status: 200 requestId HTTP creates; returned server IDs are used for 200 doing PATCH requests then 200 done PATCH requests at concurrency 8. Phase timing/CPU excludes setup and metric serialization.
methods.sql: Separate direct handler probe with existing settings and user, excluding HTTP authentication and transaction entry. Status probes roll back before the measured HTTP workload. QueryRow INSERT/UPDATE RETURNING is DML, classified from saved SQL text; Query/Exec method counts are separate.
methods.schedules: 1000 due rules and 1000 ordinary short-ID items, one production generation-helper lane, four ordinary TCP readers maintained until all rules finish without a request-count cutoff. Also 100 same-period HTTP calls racing one worker.
methods.events: 25 matching rules times 40 events, HTTP admission concurrency 8 then sequential production event transaction helpers. Four TCP readers cover complete admission and processing. Autonomous coordinator scheduling overhead is excluded.
methods.cpu: Go test CPU and allocation figures include Home plus the local HTTP client. SQLite is in the same process. PostgreSQL server CPU is excluded; no cross-provider total-CPU claim.
methods.idle: Candidate native SQLite Home process only, without a browser or active API calls in the sampling windows. Configuration happens before timing. 100Hz CPU accounting, I/O and database row counts are distinct observations. Frozen old static assets are served but no UI is exercised.
methods.profiles: No CPU or allocation profiling in this integrated round. Earlier diagnostic profiles and pure-version performance measurements remain separate historical evidence.

limits: Single-pass bounded measurements on a shared host, not an SLA, WAN latency, sustainable peak capacity or long-duration soak test.
SQLite ordinary board P95 is essentially unchanged in this sample. Fewer SQL calls and allocations, a lower median and greater throughput do not prove improved tail latency.
Bootstrap control P95 increased in both providers. This variation is retained and is not used to dismiss every change.
SQLite mixed-workload median latency increased while P95 decreased; throughput changed only modestly. All metrics are retained.
PostgreSQL data is on tmpfs with explicit 32MB/64MB min/max WAL settings. Compare only the adjacent edbd-to-candidate samples from this round, not earlier disk-backed PostgreSQL timings.
Native idle covers only the candidate SQLite Home process, not PostgreSQL background activity. Zero measured ticks or I/O does not prove absolute zero cost or independently prove zero SQL.
The old native idle, execution HTTP load, executor resource-contention matrix and notification-limit scenarios were not rerun; this integration changes query preparation and short-ID contracts.
DB connection wait is cumulative across concurrent calls and excludes earlier waiting such as the application write gate.
Every status workload retains 200 completed cycle observations with no unfinished intervals or unexpected item revisions.

No performance sample was collected during low-disk preparation. The initial launcher failed before invoking the compiler; it was corrected once and preserved separately. Both measurement binaries were then built once.
